subject: In-House Parking Operations and Technology Transition
overview: The Parking Department presented an overview of its move to in-house operations, detailing permitting requirements, enforcement policies, and new solar-powered meter technologies. Staff explained citation appeal processes and demonstrated the various mobile and physical payment methods available to residents.

items.title: Department Mission and Scope
items.summary: Director Faye Morrison introduced the department's role, clarifying that they handle civil parking enforcement exclusively while the police department manages towing and criminal matters.

items.title: Permitting and Appeals Process
items.summary: Justin detailed the requirements for residential, business, and senior permits, as well as the 21-day timeline for appealing citations online or in person.

items.title: Enforcement Policy and Strategy
items.summary: Enforcement Supervisor George Bernosky explained that the department prioritizes public safety and vehicle turnover, noting that they do not target specific vehicles upon request or enforce on private ways.

items.title: Meter Maintenance and Payment Options
items.summary: Foreman Michael Viola outlined five payment methods—coins, credit cards, telephone, website, and the PayByPhone app—and clarified that broken meters do not grant free parking.

items.title: Technology Demonstration and Closing
items.summary: Mark Burling demonstrated the interface of the new solar-powered pay stations, and Faye Morrison discussed the department's future transition to hybrid vehicles and expanded kiosk installation.
